title: Replying to @Diego Casasnovas I just wish I was more invested, but gl...
transcript: so I actually did revisit picture of Dorian Gray last week and my thoughts on it really didn't change I thought I was gonna appreciate it more the second time because I knew what I was gonna be expecting and so I could pay more attention to the story but it didn't help I kept finding myself so disconnected from the story and like don't get me wrong I love that you and others are in awe of this show I think that there is truly a show for everyone and not every show is for every person and that's very much the case with Dorian Gray it's not it's not for me I compare watching Sarah Snook in Dorian Gray to like watching your friend run a Marathon you're happy for them you think what they're doing is super impressive and you're there to cheer them on but like let's be honest you don't really care about the outcome of the Marathon you you don't really care who wins and that's how I feel about all of the characters in Dorian Gray I don't really care about the outcome of any of them it feels like I am just watching Sarah Snook get through that play as quickly as possible I'm just not invested in the characters at all in the same way that I am invested in other shows and that's kinda what I what I look for in theater is I want to be invested I wanna care about how it turns out even for shows that I've seen over and over again and this one it just it doesn't do that for me what I did appreciate more the second time is all of like the timing of everything that Sarah Snook has to hit in that show but at the same time I feel like because of how precise everything is that it kind of takes away some of the heart of the show but also one could say that that could be the point right because you are you are literally telling the story of this soulless man who sells his soul for eternal youth right and so I feel like in a way the show kinda sold its soul for the sake of just being technically impressive and I'm glad people are impressed by it I'm glad people enjoy it I will say I sat in the mezzanine the second time and my seat was a lot better so I would recommend sitting up in the mezzanine cause the boxes don't block any of the screens and I'm sure Sarah Snook is going to win the Tony because what she is doing on that stage is like really impressive right but there's just something about Laura Donnelly's performance and just Laura Donnelly walking up those steps at the end of the hills of California that's the kind of theater that like truly moves me and that's what I wanted from Dorian Gray and I just there was no point where I was moved in that same way
